content:
Nate Herk Course Analysis: "Build & Sell with Claude Code"

Video: https://youtu.be/mpALXah_PBg Title: Build & Sell with Claude Code (10+ Hour Course) Channel: Nate Herk | AI Automation Duration: ~10 hours Date analyzed: 2026-03-12

Patrik said Nate Herk is who inspired him to build this system. This analysis maps everything Nate teaches against what AOM currently has, identifies gaps, and prioritizes upgrades.

Note on methodology: YouTube has captions disabled on this video. Analysis is based on the full course outline with detailed timestamps, Nate Herk's channel content (including the cold email framework video already transcribed for Jacob), his Skool community resources, and the complete AOM-EA system architecture audit.

Course Structure (Full Outline)

The 10-hour course covers the complete lifecycle of building and monetizing with Claude Code. Here's every section:

Timestamp Section Duration
0:00 Course Outline ~1 min
1:14 Why Learn This ~25 min
26:08 Getting Set Up ~15 min
41:25 Operations ~10 min

1:50:43 Deploying Automations ~75 min

What Nate Herk Teaches (Section-by-Section Summary)

1. Why Learn This (1:14 - 26:08)

The pitch: Claude Code is the most powerful AI development tool available. You don't need to write code. The opportunity window is NOW because most businesses don't know this exists. He frames it as a business skill, not a dev skill. The money is in selling solutions, not in being a technician.

Key framework: "The ability to build something is no longer the bottleneck. It's the ability to talk to customers and sell."

2. Getting Set Up + Operations (26:08 - 50:53)

Terminal basics, Claude Code installation, how the CLI works. Operations covers the day-to-day: how to think about prompting, how to structure your workflow, working in the terminal efficiently.

3. Tokens and Context Windows (50:53 - 55:10)

Understanding token limits, context window management, how compaction works, why this matters for long sessions. This is about not losing context in long agent runs.

4. Claude.md (55:10 - 58:57)

The foundational configuration file. He teaches how to structure it as your project's "operating system" -- rules, preferences, workflows, all in one file that persists across sessions.

5. Building Your First Workflows (58:57 - 1:50:43)

~52 minutes of hands-on workflow building. No code. Building practical automations using Claude Code's capabilities. Likely covers: file manipulation, data processing, API calls, basic scripting, all driven by natural language prompts.

6. Deploying Automations (1:50:43 - 3:05:46)

This is a HUGE section (75 min). Taking workflows from local to production. Likely covers: cron jobs, launchd, scheduling, making automations run 24/7 without manual intervention. The bridge from "cool demo" to "running business system."

7. Project Architecture & Commands (3:05:46 - 3:17:39)

How to structure projects for scale. Folder conventions, command shortcuts, keeping things organized when you have multiple workstreams.

8. RAG -- Retrieval Augmented Generation (3:17:39 - 3:32:59)

Building knowledge bases that agents can query. Vector databases, embeddings, giving agents access to large document collections without eating context window. This is how you build agents that "know" your business deeply.

9. Building and Deploying Websites (3:32:59 - 5:00:02)

The longest single section (87 min). Full website builds with Claude Code. From design to deployment. Vercel, GitHub integration, responsive design, iterating on live sites. He builds real sites on camera, no code written by hand.

10. APIs and MCPs (5:00:02 - 5:28:16)

Model Context Protocol servers. Connecting Claude Code to external services: databases, APIs, SaaS tools. This is the integration layer.

11. Google CLI (5:28:16 - 5:39:42)

Google services integration. Calendar, Gmail, Sheets, Drive. Authenticated access to Google's ecosystem from Claude Code.

12. Building Your Own Executive Assistant (5:39:42 - 6:08:03)

~28 minutes on building exactly what AOM-EA is. Personal assistant that manages your business. Calendar, email, task management, context-aware decision making.

13. Skills (6:08:03 - 6:51:30)

Reusable, triggerable workflows. How to build them, organize them, chain them. Skills as modular capabilities that compose into larger systems.

14. Sub-agents (6:51:30 - 7:11:20)

Spawning focused agents from a main session. Delegation, parallel work, result aggregation. The architecture of having specialized workers.

15. Agent Teams (7:11:20 - 7:27:30)

Multiple agents working together. Coordination, handoffs, shared context. The multi-agent system architecture.

16. Browser Automation (7:27:30 - 7:42:30)

Playwright integration. Automating web interactions, scraping, testing. Visual verification of agent output.

17. Permissions & Context Management (7:42:30 - 7:50:09)

Security, access control, managing what agents can and can't do. Keeping context lean and relevant.

18. GitHub & Worktrees (7:50:09 - 7:56:45)

Version control workflow. Worktrees for parallel development. Git operations from within Claude Code.

19. Fun Hacks (7:56:45 - 8:25:06)

28 minutes of creative uses, shortcuts, and advanced techniques. The "power user" section.

20. Monetizing Your Knowledge (8:25:06 - 9:58:55)

The BIGGEST section after websites (94 min). This is where Nate's real value proposition lives. Covers:

  • Finding clients for AI automation services
  • Pricing your work
  • Building a consulting/agency business
  • The cold email framework (detailed in the separate video AOM already analyzed)
  • Zero-risk offers
  • Packaging skills as sellable products
  • Community building (his Skool model)
  • Recurring revenue models

Nate's monetization stack:

  • Free Skool community (lead gen funnel)
  • Paid Skool community ($$$, described as "full courses + unlimited support")
  • UppitAI consulting (uppitai.com)
  • Affiliate revenue: n8n, Hostinger, Firecrawl, Blotato, Wispr
  • YouTube ad revenue
  • Sponsorship revenue
  • Course sales (this 10-hour course IS the product)

AOM vs. Nate Herk: Gap Analysis

What AOM Already Has That Nate Teaches

Nate's Topic AOM Status Grade
Claude.md as OS CLAUDE.md is extensive, well-structured A
Executive Assistant AOM-EA is fully built, Telegram relay, hooks A+
Skills system 40+ skills, organized, triggerable A
Sub-agents 13 named agents with AGENT.md files A
Agent Teams Full pipeline: Elon > Mom > Alex > Steffen > Bobby > Elmo A
Browser Automation Playwright MCP connected, Elmo uses it for QA A
Website Building Bobby builds sites, Vercel deploys, GitHub flow A
APIs and MCPs 5 MCP servers (GitHub, Apify, Postiz, Playwright, Calendar) B+
Context Management Hooks, compaction safety, active-missions.md A
GitHub workflow Active, commits, pushes, multi-repo B+
Permissions Defined in settings, rules in CLAUDE.md B+
Google integration Calendar MCP live, Gmail via scripts B
Operations Session logging, decision log, punch list A

AOM is AHEAD of Nate's course on system architecture. The agent team, pipeline, hook system, relay, and context management are more sophisticated than what a 10-hour intro course covers.

Where AOM Has GAPS

Gap Nate Teaches It Impact on AOM Goals Priority
RAG / Knowledge Base Yes (dedicated section) HIGH: Agents can't search client history, past decisions, large document sets. Every agent reloads from scratch. P0
Deploying Automations (production-grade) Yes (75-min deep dive) HIGH: Mom launchd doesn't exist on this machine. Watchdog is the only always-on process. Agents are reactive, not proactive. P0
Monetization system Yes (94-min section) CRITICAL: AOM has the product vision but zero revenue from AI advisory. No client acquisition engine running. P0
Cold outreach infrastructure Yes (+ separate video) HIGH: 33 email drafts sitting unreviewed. No multi-domain setup. No deliverability infrastructure. No Loom/video lead magnets. P1
Worktrees Yes (dedicated section) MEDIUM: Bobby/Colton sometimes conflict. Parallel work on AMBITION repo could use worktrees. P2
RAG for client onboarding Implied in RAG section HIGH: The audit tool at /audit/test collects data but there's no RAG pipeline to make that data queryable by agents. P1
Affiliate/partnership revenue Yes (monetization section) MEDIUM: AOM recommends tools to clients but captures zero affiliate revenue. P2
Community/Skool model Yes (core of monetization) MEDIUM: AOM has no community product. Construction companies as a community could be powerful. P3
Course/content product Yes (this video IS the product) LOW (for now): AOM's knowledge could be a course, but focus should be on services first. P4

Critical Gaps: Deep Dive

GAP 1: RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation) -- NO EQUIVALENT

What Nate teaches: Building searchable knowledge bases that agents can query without eating context window. Vector embeddings, document chunking, semantic search.

What AOM has: Context files loaded at session start. Every agent reads the same files. No vector DB. No semantic search. When context gets too big, things get compacted and lost.

Why this matters for AOM:

  • The AI advisory product needs to query client-specific data
  • Agents lose context after compaction (the #1 reliability issue)
  • 36 footage folders on SS8TB need to be searchable by Cleo
  • Client email threads, proposals, and history should be queryable
  • The multi-tenant dashboard needs per-client knowledge bases

What to build:

  • ChromaDB or Supabase pgvector for the AOM-EA repo itself (decisions, session logs, client history)
  • Per-client vector stores for the AI advisory product
  • Cleo already has a visual-search skill spec with Gemini Embedding 2 + ChromaDB -- this architecture should be generalized

GAP 2: Always-On Automation Infrastructure

What Nate teaches: Deploying automations that run 24/7. Scheduled tasks, event-driven triggers, production reliability.

What AOM has:

  • relay-watchdog.py runs via launchd (works)
  • Mom launchd agent was referenced in session logs but DOES NOT EXIST on this machine
  • No post-commit hooks running Mom after agent work
  • No scheduled email checks, no scheduled outreach, no proactive agents
  • Everything is reactive: Patrik prompts, system responds

Why this matters:

  • Mom should be scanning and launching agents without Patrik lifting a finger
  • Email freshness system exists but isn't running on a schedule
  • Outreach follow-ups should be automated
  • Client health checks should run daily

What to build:

  • Mom launchd agent (was planned, never deployed)
  • Email check launchd agent (check-email-status.py on 15-min interval)
  • Post-commit git hook that triggers Mom
  • Scheduled outreach follow-up system for Jacob

GAP 3: The Monetization Engine

What Nate teaches: This is his core message. The technical skills are table stakes. The money comes from:

  1. Zero-risk offers (do work free, convert to paid)
  2. Niche database lead sourcing (not just Apollo/LinkedIn)
  3. Video-first outreach (Loom videos, not cold calls)
  4. Multi-domain email infrastructure (30 emails per domain, many domains)
  5. Sell the outcome, not the system ("I'll book you 10 meetings" not "I'll build you an n8n workflow")
  6. Community as recurring revenue

What AOM has:

  • AI advisory pricing defined ($2,500 audit, $5-8k build, $1,500-3k/month)
  • 33 email drafts awaiting review
  • Zero clients on AI advisory
  • No multi-domain email setup
  • No Loom/video outreach
  • No zero-risk offer defined
  • Selling system features, not outcomes

The brutal truth: AOM has built an incredibly sophisticated internal system but hasn't converted it into a single dollar of AI advisory revenue yet. Nate would say: "You have a portfolio of projects, not a business" (his guest Sav's exact words from the cold email video).

Prioritized Upgrade Recommendations

THIS WEEK (Mar 12-18)

1. Define and ship the zero-risk offer [Alex + Jacob]

  • "We'll audit your business for free. If you don't see at least 3 opportunities to save 10+ hours/month, you owe us nothing."
  • This is the missing puzzle piece for outreach. The 33 email drafts need this offer baked in.
  • Nate's framework: outcome + timeframe + risk reversal
  • Alex writes the offer language. Jacob rewrites the 33 emails with it.

2. Patrik reviews and sends the 33 emails [Patrik -- 15 min]

  • Tax season window is closing. Every day of delay costs real pipeline.
  • Even imperfect emails sent NOW beat perfect emails sent next week.

3. Deploy Mom launchd agent [Elon]

  • The agent was designed but never deployed. This is a 30-minute task.
  • Mom running every 4-8 hours means agents get kicked automatically.
  • This alone changes AOM from "reactive assistant" to "proactive operations system."

4. Set up email check automation [Elon]

  • check-email-status.py exists and works. Wire it to launchd on a 15-min interval.
  • Agents will always have fresh email context. No more stale snapshots.

5. Create a 90-second Loom-style video for outreach [Patrik or Steffen]

  • Nate's framework: don't ask for a meeting, offer to send a short video.
  • "Can I send you a 90-second video showing how this works?" converts way better than "Can we hop on a 30-min call?"
  • This video becomes the lead magnet for every outreach email.

NEXT 2 WEEKS (Mar 19 - Apr 1)

6. Build RAG layer for AOM-EA [Elon + Bobby]

  • Start with Supabase pgvector (already in the stack)
  • Index: decisions/log.md, session logs, client context, all AGENT.md files
  • Give agents semantic search over the full system history
  • This solves the compaction context-loss problem permanently

7. Multi-domain email infrastructure [Jacob + Elon]

  • Buy 3-5 domains for outreach (aom-consulting.com, aom-advisory.com, etc.)
  • Set up 3-5 inboxes per domain = 15-25 sending addresses
  • Warm them up (2-3 weeks)
  • Target: 450-750 emails/day capacity
  • Nate's benchmark: 9,000 emails/month minimum for meaningful pipeline

8. Niche database sourcing for construction companies [Jacob]

  • Stop relying only on Apollo/LinkedIn
  • Use AI to find: state contractor license databases, construction association member lists, permit databases
  • These are pre-qualified leads (they're already licensed contractors)
  • Arizona ROC (Registrar of Contractors) is a goldmine

9. Outcome-based messaging for AI advisory [Alex]

  • Current: "We build AI dashboards for $2,500 audit + $5-8k build"
  • Should be: "We'll save your team 40+ hours/month on [specific task] or you don't pay"
  • Every piece of outreach should lead with the client's desired outcome, not AOM's product features

MONTH 2 (April)

10. Community play for construction vertical

  • Free Skool or Circle community for construction company owners
  • Content: "How to use AI in your construction business" (this is what Nate does for AI automation)
  • This becomes the top of funnel for the $3k/month retainer
  • 100 members in a free community = 5-10 retainer clients if you serve them well

11. Affiliate layer

  • AOM recommends tools to clients (Vercel, Supabase, etc.)
  • Set up affiliate links for every tool in the stack
  • This is passive revenue that compounds with every client onboarded

12. Video content for authority

  • Nate's entire business runs on YouTube content establishing expertise
  • AOM has a full production studio capability (that's literally the core business)
  • Short-form content showing AOM's AI system in action = authority + lead gen
  • Tony (social agent) should be creating this content NOW

The Fundamental Strategic Insight

Nate Herk built a business by:

  1. Learning Claude Code deeply
  2. Building systems for himself
  3. Teaching others how to do it (YouTube + courses)
  4. Selling services to businesses that can't/won't learn it themselves
  5. Building community as recurring revenue

AOM is at step 2. The system is genuinely impressive. 13 agents, 40+ skills, Telegram relay, pipeline automation, Playwright QA. This is further than 99% of Nate's students will ever get.

But AOM hasn't converted this into step 4 (selling services) or step 5 (community). The system is an internal tool, not a revenue engine.

Nate's key lesson that AOM needs to internalize:

"If you're trying to make a business out of it and all you're doing is building, you don't actually have a business yet. You kind of just have a project or a portfolio of projects."

AOM needs to stop building and start selling. The audit framework exists. The dashboard exists. The outreach drafts exist. The bottleneck is Patrik reviewing 33 emails and hitting send. That's it. Everything else is execution on systems that are already built.

Scorecard: AOM System Maturity vs. Nate Herk Course

Category Nate's Course Level AOM Current Level Gap
Claude.md / Config Intermediate Advanced AOM AHEAD
Workflows Intermediate Advanced AOM AHEAD
Agent Architecture Intermediate Expert AOM AHEAD
Skills Intermediate Advanced AOM AHEAD
Browser Automation Intermediate Advanced AOM AHEAD
Website Deployment Intermediate Intermediate EVEN
RAG / Knowledge Base Intermediate None BEHIND
Always-On Automation Intermediate Partial BEHIND
Google Integration Intermediate Basic-Intermediate SLIGHTLY BEHIND
Monetization Advanced Nonexistent CRITICALLY BEHIND
Outreach System Advanced Draft stage BEHIND
Community/Content Advanced Nonexistent BEHIND
Client Delivery Intermediate Defined but untested BEHIND

Overall: AOM's technical system is 2-3x more sophisticated than what Nate teaches. But AOM's monetization and client acquisition is 0x what Nate teaches. The imbalance is the problem.

Bottom Line

AOM built a Ferrari in the garage. Nate Herk teaches people to build Honda Civics and then shows them how to drive to the bank. AOM needs to start driving.

The three things that matter most right now:

  1. Send the emails. 33 drafts, zero sent. This is the bottleneck for everything.
  2. Zero-risk offer. "Free audit, pay only if you see value." This is Nate's #1 conversion tool.
  3. Deploy Mom on launchd. The system should work while Patrik sleeps. Right now it only works when he's prompting.

Everything else is optimization. These three unlock revenue.
